subject: Life Skills
title: Eat the Frog First
description: Learn Eat the Frog First in one minute.

hook.text: Mark Twain supposedly said: if you eat a live frog first thing in the morning, nothing worse can happen all day.

buildup.text: The 'frog' is the task you dread most — usually the most important one you keep pushing to tomorrow.

discovery.text: Willpower peaks in the morning and depletes as the day goes on. Your frog deserves your freshest energy.

twist.text: People start with easy tasks to 'warm up.' But those small wins drain the energy meant for the hard one.

climax.text: Identify your frog the night before. When morning comes, attack it before checking email or social media.

punchline.text: Eat the frog at dawn. The rest of the day is easy.

quiz.question: Why should you tackle your hardest task first?
options: Willpower is highest in the morning and fades through the day
Coworkers are less likely to interrupt early
